narr: Severe thunderstorms moved across Mississippi during the evening and overnight hours of the 13th into the 14th, with flash flooding across areas of the Delta and several tornadoes. Severe storm coverage diminished during the night, but storms became severe again during the afternoon of the 14th as a cold front interacted with a warm and unstable air mass in the region. Tornadoes on the 14th were generally along and south of the Interstate 20 corridor with severe storms continuing into the evening.
ev: Heavy rain from thunderstorms produced an area of flash flooding in eastern Lamar County. Slade and Whiddon roads had water across them and cars were stalled with water rescues necessary along Hardy Street in West Hattiesburg. Homes were impacted by high water in the area.
Portions of Swilley Road were washed out.
Several bridges were inundated with flood water in Adams county, including on Bourke Road.

Heavy rain with thunderstorms across Hattiesburg resulted in numerous reports of flash flooding, with homes and vehicles impacted by high water. Water rescues from stalled vehicles occurred along Hardy street with Mcleod street and Main streets blocked due to high water, flooding along Mamie street, with reports of flooding across numerous other roads across town including near Providence Street and Old highway 42.
Heavy rainfall caused flash flooding county wide, including Greenville, Leland, Hollandale and Metcalfe.

Heavy rain resulted in about 10 inches of flowing water across Ridgewood Road.
